gap: No result ChatGPT got says what computer the higher-end scanners need: Creality's CR-Scan Raptor manual recommends an NVIDIA card with 6 GB of video memory on Windows, or an Apple M1/M2/M3 Mac on macOS 11.7.7 or later with 16 GB of RAM, and Einstar says its software supports only Apple Silicon Macs (M1 or later, macOS Ventura 13 or later, 16 GB RAM required) and Windows PCs with NVIDIA graphics.
standout_why: I read the two pages ChatGPT cited (3dprinting.com/3d-scanners/ and 3dprinting.com/scanners/best-small-format-3d-scanners/) and the top result (printingxyz.com/articles/best-3d-scanners-2026/). Their only compatibility notes are: the Ferret SE runs on Windows or Mac with no phone support, the Ferret Pro and Raptor have Wi-Fi 6, the Einstar 2 and VEGA are wireless, and the POP 3 Plus connects to a phone or PC over USB. None mentions NVIDIA, CUDA, video memory, Apple Silicon or Intel Macs, or RAM for any scanner. The closest any of them gets is the line 'a real RTX-class workstation outperforms onboard hardware'.
decides: ChatGPT's 'best for mechanical parts' pick, the Creality CR-Scan Raptor ($879), and our Einstar VEGA row both assume a strong computer: an NVIDIA card or an Apple Silicon Mac with 16 GB of RAM. A shopper with an Intel Mac or a laptop without NVIDIA graphics falls outside what these makers state they support. The page should put a 'computer you need' line next to each pick and steer those shoppers to scanners that also run on a phone (our INSPIRE 2 row lists phone or PC over USB-C or Wi-Fi 6). This doesn't change the pick for someone with an RTX PC or an M-series Mac.

findings.label: Recommended Windows PC
findings.value: i7 7th-gen CPU, NVIDIA graphics card with 6 GB VRAM, 16 GB RAM
findings.source_title: Creality CR-SCAN RAPTOR manual, page 9 (ManualsLib copy)
findings.note: Wording on the page: 'Recommended configuration: i7-Gen7 CPU, Nvidia graphics card (6GB VRAM)'. The manual calls this recommended, not minimum. The RAM line is cut off in the OCR text, so 16 GB comes from the same sentence and from Creality's macOS line. Creality's own wiki pages render with JavaScript and returned no text.
